ai.description: This gecko reaches 8 cm SVL. It is brownish-grey with dark transverse dorsal bands and a pale, unpatterned venter. Distinctive features include a slender, curved tail and strongly bent digits.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus khasiensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark nuchal loop that connects behind the eyes, unlike the broken patterns of its kin.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus khasiensis* inhabits moist, subtropical broadleaf forests and rocky outcrops within the Khasi Hills, typically at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Khasi Hills bent-toed gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects along rocky outcrops and tree trunks within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus khasiensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus khasiensis* is endemic to the Khasi and Jaintia Hills of Meghalaya, India, typically inhabiting forested regions at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
